explanation: At equilibrium the concentrations of products and reactants are related by the equilibrium constant K, written as products over reactants each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient; for A + B <-> C this is K = [C]/([A][B]). K > 1 means the equilibrium lies toward products, K < 1 means it favors reactants, and K depends only on temperature, not on the starting amounts. Comparing the reaction quotient Q to K tells you which way a reaction shifts (Q < K shifts right toward products). On the AP exam you build K expressions from balanced equations, exclude pure solids and liquids, and use ICE tables to solve for unknown concentrations. The bars show each species' concentration and the live readout recomputes K as you change them.
bullets: K = [products]/[reactants], each to its coefficient: here [C]/([A][B]).
K > 1 favors products; K < 1 favors reactants (shown live).
K depends only on temperature, not on initial concentrations.
Bars are [A], [B], [C]; the readout recomputes K from them each frame.
